lessons.title: OOP without inheritance is inefficient
lessons.interactiveContent:
When we create objects one by one we run into the problem of having duplicate code. How many greet() methods are there?

31

Make sure to pick 3.
lessons.hardModeContent:
When you create separate classes, you can end up with duplicate code, as with these three greet methods.

You change only Person1.greet to print Hello. What will the other two methods print?

Both still print Hi! because their method bodies are separateBoth print Hello because methods with the same name share their codeBoth stop working because matching method names must print matching text

Both still print Hi! because their method bodies are separate.

lessons.title: The concept of inheritance
lessons.interactiveContent: We use inheritance to make our code efficient. Through inheritance, classes receive methods from other classes.

lessons.title: The concept of inheritance 2
lessons.interactiveContent: Inheritance lets us create classes that have different properties and behaviors without coding each one from scratch.

lessons.title: The concept of inheritance 3
lessons.interactiveContent: Here we see that the Child class is inheriting the Parent class because it's inside the parentheses after the class name.

lessons.title: Creating objects that inherit methods
lessons.interactiveContent:
Let's look at how a class can inherit methods from another. When defining the class we add parentheses with the class that we're inheriting.

Make sure to pick (, followed by Greetings, and finally ).
lessons.hardModeContent:
To inherit methods, you put the other class name in parentheses after your new class name.

Make Person inherit from Greetings.

Make sure to pick (, followed by Greetings, and finally ).

lessons.title: Calling inherited methods
lessons.interactiveContent:
The Person class can now use the Greeting's methods like its own. Try calling greet() as a method of person.

Make sure to pick . followed by greet and then (, ).
lessons.hardModeContent:
The Person class can use inherited methods as its own.

Call the inherited method on p so the console shows Hi!.

Make sure to pick ., followed by greet, (, and finally ).

lessons.interactiveContent:
We can update how classes work by setting methods directly in the class. Define the charge method inside the Hybrid class.

Make sure to pick def followed by charge and then (, self, ), :.
lessons.hardModeContent:

Give Hybrid its own charge method so the console shows Starting car then Using fuel to charge battery.

Use self as the first parameter.

lessons.title: Outro
lessons.interactiveContent: We've learned how flexible Python can be using inheritance. Next, we'll dive further into how classes inherit things.

lessons.title: Question 1
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which of these describes inheritance?

Classes that inherit the functionality of another classClasses that only inherit variables from other classes

Classes that inherit the functionality of another class.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Inheritance allows a class to inherit the functionality of another class.

A Hybrid class inherits from Car. Why can a Hybrid object call start_car()?

The child class inherits that functionality from CarA child class can inherit only variables, so the method must be globalEvery object can call every method defined anywhere in the programCreating the child object rewrites start_car() inside Hybrid

The child class inherits that functionality from Car.

lessons.title: Question 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
How does inheritance make our OOP code more efficient?

Functions need to be set only onceProperties need to be set only once

Functions need to be set only once.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Inheritance makes OOP code more efficient because shared functions need to be set only once.

Three child classes need the same greet() behavior. Where should that function be defined?

Once in their shared parent classSeparately in every child classAs a property in each objectInside only the first child class

Once in their shared parent class.

lessons.title: Question 3
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which of these doesn't need to be inherited?

Methods used by only one objectMethods used by more than one object

Methods used by only one object.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Methods used by more than one object can be inherited, while a method used by only one object does not need to be inherited.

Only the Bird child class needs fly(). Where should that method stay?

In Bird, because the other child classes do not need itIn the parent, so every child inherits unused behaviorIn every child class, even though only Bird uses itOutside all classes because unique methods cannot belong to a child class

In Bird, because the other child classes do not need it.

lessons.title: Question 4
lessons.interactiveContent:
How can inheritance improve the code?

We can avoid unnecessary repetition of codeNothing can be improved

We can avoid unnecessary repetition of code.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Inheritance can improve code by avoiding unnecessary repetition.

Both car classes define the same drive() method, but their other methods differ. Which refactor fits the code?

Move drive() to a parent class and keep each unique method in its childKeep both copies because methods cannot be inheritedMove brake() and reverse() to the parent because every child needs themMake RedCar inherit from BlueCar only to reuse drive()

Move drive() to a parent class and keep each unique method in its child.

A child instance can call methods inherited from its parent and methods defined in its own class.

The jet object is an instance of Jet(Plane). Which pair of calls is available on it?

Both jet.fly() and jet.invert()Only jet.fly() because child methods are not available on instancesOnly jet.invert() because parent methods are not inheritedNeither method because Jet does not define an initializer

Both jet.fly() and jet.invert().
